title: Contraction-ordering ladder
summary: A seeded hard-instance set of 4-8 matrix chains and 3-6 tensor networks, scoring the non-learned contraction-ordering players (one-step oracle, greedy episode, saturation, classic greedy) by cost and rank against the exact DP optimum.

findings.claim: a learned search policy can beat greedy on contraction-ordering *quality*
findings.headline: no — the priced rule space already reaches the DP optimum: saturate ties optimal on 60/60 chains; the residual headroom above greedy is search cost, not quality
findings.metric: saturate chains at the DP optimum

findings.claim: full equality saturation reaches the exact contraction-ordering DP optimum on matrix chains
findings.headline: saturate == 2·DP optimum on 60/60 chains (worst ratio 1.000)

findings.claim: the one-step greedy cost-model oracle is optimal on contraction ordering
findings.headline: one-step oracle at the optimum on 38/60 chains (63%); mean ratio 1.28, worst 4.09x
findings.metric: one-step oracle chains at optimum / n

findings.claim: the multi-step greedy episode is optimal on contraction ordering
findings.headline: greedy episode (h6/p2) at the optimum on 59/60 chains vs one-step 38/60; worst 1.01x
findings.metric: greedy episode chains at optimum / n

findings.claim: classic greedy is optimal on general tensor networks
findings.headline: classic greedy at the optimum on 20/60 networks (33%); mean ratio 1.57, worst 5.5x
findings.metric: classic greedy networks at optimum / n
